**Life‑expectancy at birth (total, both sexes) – most recent World Bank / UN data (2022‑2023)**  

| Rank (by population) | Country | Approx. population (2023) | Life expectancy* (years) |
|-----------------------|---------|---------------------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **China** | ~1.41 billion | **78.5 yr** |
| 2 | **India** | ~1.40 billion | **70.9 yr** |
| 3 | **United States** | ~332 million | **77.0 yr** |
| 4 | **Indonesia** | ~276 million | **73.7 yr** |

\* *Life expectancy figures are the most recent “total” (both‑sex) values published by the World Bank (World Development Indicators) and the United Nations World Population Prospects (2022 revision). They reflect “period life expectancy at birth” – the average number of years a newborn would live if the age‑specific mortality rates of the reference year remained constant throughout its life.*

### How the numbers are derived  

| Source | Year of estimate | Methodology |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **World Bank – World Development Indicators** | 2022 (latest released) | Period life expectancy at birth, compiled from national statistical offices and UN demographic databases. |
| **UN World Population Prospects (2022 revision)** | 2022 | Period life expectancy at birth, based on UN‑compiled vital‑registration and survey data. |

Both organisations publish the same “total” figure (averaging male and female life expectancy). The values above are rounded to the nearest tenth of a year, which is the precision used in the official tables.

### Quick context  

| Country | Life expectancy (years) | Comparison to global average (≈73 yr, 2022) |
|---------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| **China** | 78.5 | +5.5 yr (well above average) |
| **India** | 70.9 | –2.1 yr (slightly below average) |
| **United States** | 77.0 | +4.0 yr (well above average) |
| **Indonesia** | 73.7 | +0.7 yr (just above average) |

These figures give a snapshot of the health‑outcome status of the four most‑populous nations as of the latest internationally‑reported data.  

**References**  

1. World Bank, *World Development Indicators* – “Life expectancy at birth, total (years)”, data downloaded 2024.  
2. United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* – Table 2.1, “Life expectancy at birth (years)”.
